item.title: Benn Jordan Testifies on Flock Safety ALPR Surveillance
item.description:
Benn Jordan Testifies on Flock Safety ALPR Surveillance

Benn Jordan, musician‑turned‑investigative journalist, has become a leading voice exposing the private‑sector surveillance network built around Flock Safety’s automatic license‑plate readers (ALPRs).

🔎 Overview

  • Jordan has shifted from an experimental music career to investigating Flock Safety’s ALPR systems.
  • His work has prompted congressional testimony, government scrutiny, and contract cancellations.

🎤 Who is Benn Jordan

  • Musician, YouTuber, researcher, and investigative journalist.
  • Known for a prolific discography of experimental music dating back decades.
  • In the last couple of years, he has become a high‑profile face in creator and media spaces for his work investigating Flock Safety.

📡 Flock Safety’s ALPR Network

  • Flock manufactures automatic license‑plate readers and the software that powers them.
  • Atlanta has more Flock cameras than anywhere else per square mile.
  • Jordan first noticed the cameras about two years ago, initially thinking they were traffic cameras.

🏛️ Congressional Testimony and Political Response

  • Jordan recently testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee’s Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism on Flock and other ALPR systems.
  • Hundreds of cities, counties, and other local governments have begun canceling contracts with Flock.
  • Republican Senator Josh Hawley has opened an investigation into Flock.

📉 Business Impact

  • Reuters reported that Flock plans to cut about 18 percent of its workforce.

🛠️ Jordan’s Accountability Approach

  • He does not hate Flock as a company; he says its posture toward critics is a PR failure.
  • He talks directly to Flock’s CEO Garrett Langley and reports security vulnerabilities when he finds them.
  • His YouTube videos and collaborations with other researchers, civil‑rights groups, and journalists serve as an accountability function that forces the conversation to the forefront.

📢 Why It Matters

  • The issue extends beyond Flock to the interlocking relationship between private industry, government, and law enforcement that prioritizes secrecy over transparency.
  • Lack of transparency allows a network of cameras to be deployed without public consent, raising concerns about abuse by police officers.
  • Jordan emphasizes that society never voted for an insecure network of cameras on every street corner.

#Surveillance #Privacy #ALPR #Congress #FlockSafety

Source: Benn Jordan thinks the surveillance problem is much bigger than Flock

item.title: Lawmakers Hold Hearing on Flock AI Surveillance Network and ALPRs
item.description:
Lawmakers Hold Hearing on Flock AI Surveillance Network and ALPRs

Washington lawmakers recently held a hearing to examine the “AI Surveillance Network” operated by Flock and the use of automated license plate readers (ALPRs). While the CEOs of Flock and peer companies Axon, Motorola Solutions, and Verkada declined to testify, the hearing featured testimony from legal and cybersecurity experts, a sheriff, and a private citizen.

⚙️ Key details

Lawmakers expressed several specific concerns regarding the technology and its implementation:

  • Data Collection: Concerns were raised about ALPRs that “hoover up location data for Americans who haven’t been accused of crimes,” with information sometimes stored for a full month.
  • Security: Cybersecurity engineer Benn Jordan testified that he previously accessed Flock’s image trove with “minimal technical maneuvering,” though he noted security has improved from a year ago.
  • Access and Use: Lawmakers questioned the ease of officer access to data and the ability of the system to construct dossiers on individual vehicles, which they noted is distinct from traditional license plate readers.
  • Legal Loopholes: Senators Alex Padilla and Dick Durbin questioned how federal immigration authorities could be barred from the data, with one witness suggesting a sympathetic local officer could perform searches on their behalf.
  • Civil Liberties: Sen. Cory Booker asked if the technology could be used to track people seeking reproductive care across state lines, while Sen. Josh Hawley noted similar risks for gun owners near ranges or stores.

💡 Why it matters

Testimony from the hearing highlighted the real-world impact of the technology, including a Florida woman who stated she spent 13 days in jail after Flock cameras incorrectly identified her car as being connected to a crime scene. Additionally, one sheriff testified that his department ended its contract with Flock after receiving “slippery answers” regarding its AI use.

Company Position/Response
Flock CEO declined to testify at the hearing.
Verkada Spokesperson Virginia Ramsey stated that no national Verkada network exists and customers only access data in their own systems.
Axon CEO declined to testify.
Motorola Solutions CEO declined to testify.

#Flock #AISurveillance #ALPR #Privacy #PublicSafety

Source: The vibes are bad for Flock in Washington
